name: Planning Accessibility and Aging-in-Place Features in LA ADUs

mainEntity.name: What accessibility and aging-in-place features should I ask an ADU design contractor to incorporate for future flexibility in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What accessibility and aging-in-place features should I ask an ADU design contractor to incorporate for future flexibility in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even if you are not building a fully ADA-compliant unit, it is smart to design ADUs in Los Angeles County with aging-in-place in mind. Ask your ADU design contractor to create at least one no-step entrance, which may require grading, a gentle ramp, or careful placement relative to the main house. Doors should typically be 32–36 inches clear width, with hallways wide enough for potential wheelchair or walker use. In the bathroom, specify a curbless or low-threshold shower, reinforce walls with blocking for future grab bars, and ensure enough space for side transfers by a person with mobility challenges. Lever-style door hardware and faucets are easier for people with limited hand strength. In the kitchen, consider lower countertop sections, drawers instead of deep base cabinets, and room for seated work areas. Ask your designer to confirm wheelchair turning radii in bathrooms, bedrooms, and the main living area, even if you do not need them immediately. These features add relatively modest cost when integrated from the start and can significantly increase the ADU’s long-term usability and rental appeal, especially in a market where multigenerational living and senior rentals are growing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Request features like a no-step entrance, wider doors and halls, curbless shower, blocking for grab bars, lever handles, and space for future ramps or lifts. Ask your ADU design contractor to design clear wheelchair turning radii in key rooms and to plan for at least one bedroom and bathroom on one level.
